assessments.technical_explanation: A pre-commit hook runs type checking, formatting, linting, and tests by launching the local npm CLI. It reads one environment variable for output length and passes the current environment to the local child process so npm works normally. Environment values are never serialized to storage, embedded in output, or sent over a network. The only child processes are git and npm against the local repository, matching the tooling purpose. The environment is also only ever used locally by the developer running the hook, not by extension users.
